_comment: Source manifest for the Academic-Reading starter corpus. 'copyright': PD = public domain, FD = in copyright, used as a short fair-dealing excerpt. Five entries were removed in v1.1 because the text could not be obtained — see manifest.json 'dropped'. The finished excerpts live in <lang>/<id>.txt; this file records where they came from.

texts.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
texts.title: Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei — I. Bourgeois und Proletarier
texts.excerpt_note: Take from the opening ('Die Geschichte aller bisherigen Gesellschaft...') through the account of the bourgeoisie's revolutionising of production.

texts.author: Otto von Bismarck
texts.title: Reichstagsrede vom 6. Februar 1888
texts.excerpt_note: The closing section containing 'Wir Deutsche fürchten Gott, sonst nichts auf der Welt'.

texts.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
texts.title: Zur Genealogie der Moral — Erste Abhandlung, §§ 1–5
texts.excerpt_note: Sections 1-5 of the first treatise (Gut und Böse / Gut und Schlecht).

texts.author: Ferdinand Tönnies
texts.title: Gemeinschaft und Gesellschaft — Buch I, Einleitung
texts.excerpt_note: The opening definition of Gemeinschaft against Gesellschaft.

texts.author: Georg Simmel
texts.title: Die Großstädte und das Geistesleben
texts.excerpt_note: Opening through the discussion of Blasiertheit and the money economy.

texts.author: Rosa Luxemburg
texts.title: Die russische Revolution — Demokratie und Diktatur
texts.excerpt_note: The chapter containing 'Freiheit ist immer die Freiheit des Andersdenkenden'. Follow the chapter link from the index page.

texts.author: Max Weber
texts.title: Politik als Beruf — Schluss (Gesinnungsethik und Verantwortungsethik)
texts.excerpt_note: From the introduction of Gesinnungsethik vs Verantwortungsethik to the 'Dennoch!' ending.

texts.author: Sigmund Freud
texts.title: Das Unbehagen in der Kultur — Kapitel II

resolve.query: Freud Das Unbehagen in der Kultur

texts.excerpt_note: The discussion of what people demand of life and the three sources of suffering.

texts.author: Theodor W. Adorno
texts.title: Erziehung nach Auschwitz
texts.excerpt_note: Opening pages. Widely anthologised; take a ~1000-word excerpt from a copy you hold.

texts.author: Richard von Weizsäcker
texts.title: Rede zum 40. Jahrestag der Beendigung des Krieges, 8. Mai 1985
texts.excerpt_note: Officially published by the Bundespräsidialamt. The section on remembrance ('Der 8. Mai war ein Tag der Befreiung').

texts.author: Oswald Spengler
texts.title: Der Untergang des Abendlandes — Einleitung
texts.excerpt_note: The opening statement of the morphology of world history.

texts.author: Alexis de Tocqueville
texts.title: L'Ancien Régime et la Révolution — Livre III, ch. IV
texts.excerpt_note: Why prosperity and reform hastened the Revolution.

texts.author: Ernest Renan
texts.title: Qu'est-ce qu'une nation ?
texts.excerpt_note: The closing third: nation as spiritual principle and 'un plébiscite de tous les jours'.

texts.author: Jules Ferry
texts.title: Discours sur la politique coloniale, 28 juillet 1885

resolve.query: Jules Ferry discours 28 juillet 1885 politique coloniale

texts.excerpt_note: The 'races supérieures' passage with Clemenceau's interruptions — excellent for rhetorical analysis.

texts.author: Émile Durkheim
texts.title: Les règles de la méthode sociologique — ch. I
texts.excerpt_note: The definition of the fait social.

texts.author: Émile Zola
texts.title: J'accuse… ! (Lettre à M. Félix Faure)
texts.excerpt_note: The final anaphoric section is the set piece; include enough preceding context to make it coherent.

texts.author: Paul Valéry
texts.title: La crise de l'esprit — première lettre
texts.excerpt_note: Opens 'Nous autres, civilisations, nous savons maintenant que nous sommes mortelles.'

texts.author: Marcel Mauss
texts.title: Essai sur le don — Introduction
texts.excerpt_note: The programme: gift, obligation, reciprocity, fait social total.

texts.author: Simone de Beauvoir
texts.title: Le Deuxième Sexe — Introduction
texts.excerpt_note: Opening of the introduction ('Qu'est-ce qu'une femme ?').

texts.author: Carlo Cattaneo
texts.title: La città considerata come principio ideale delle istorie italiane

resolve.query: Cattaneo La città considerata come principio ideale delle istorie italiane

texts.excerpt_note: The opening argument that the city, not the state, is the constant of Italian history.

texts.author: Giuseppe Mazzini
texts.title: I doveri dell'uomo — Doveri verso la Patria
texts.excerpt_note: The chapter on duties towards the Patria.

texts.author: Camillo Benso di Cavour
texts.title: Discorso su Roma capitale, 25 marzo 1861
texts.excerpt_note: Parliamentary oratory at the moment of unification.

texts.author: Cesare Lombroso
texts.title: L'uomo delinquente — il delinquente nato
texts.excerpt_note: The atavism thesis. Historically enormous, scientifically discredited — good critical-reading material.

texts.author: Gaetano Mosca
texts.title: Elementi di scienza politica — la classe politica
texts.excerpt_note: The founding statement of elite theory.

texts.author: Vilfredo Pareto
texts.title: Manuale di economia politica — ofelimità ed equilibrio
texts.excerpt_note: Choose a passage light on formal notation.

texts.author: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti
texts.title: Fondazione e Manifesto del Futurismo

resolve.title: I Manifesti del futurismo/Fondazione e Manifesto del futurismo

texts.excerpt_note: Short enough to use nearly whole — the eleven points plus surrounding frame.

texts.author: Benedetto Croce
texts.title: Manifesto degli intellettuali antifascisti
texts.excerpt_note: Roughly 1000 words as written — usable entire.

texts.author: Antonio Gramsci
texts.title: Quaderni del carcere — Gli intellettuali
texts.excerpt_note: The organic intellectual. Prison-notebook prose is compressed — keep a whole note as the unit.

texts.author: Umberto Eco
texts.title: Il fascismo eterno
texts.excerpt_note: The enumerated features of Ur-Fascism — a gift for teaching argumentative structure.

texts.author: 嚴復 Yan Fu
texts.title: 論世變之亟
texts.excerpt_note: The contrast between Chinese and Western civilisation after the defeat by Japan.

texts.author: 梁啟超 Liang Qichao
texts.title: 少年中國說
